text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- U.S. company General Motors wants to operate its own railway engine maintenance plant in the Pila-based rolling stock maintenance plant run by Polish State Railways (PKP) in western Poland, Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said.

- Opel wants to enter Poland's small passenger car market and compete with the dominant Fiat Cinquecento model, Adam Opel AG president David Herman said. He said that at the end of 1998 it would introduce a new mini-type car which will be 20 percent cheaper than the presently-offered Corsa model.
- Waldemar Pawlak and Roman Jagielinski have confirmed that they will compete for the leadership of the co-ruling Polish Peasant Party (PSL) at the party congress in November.

- Poland's acting finance minister Janusz Kaczurba and Polish Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ) representatives will participate in a three-day Poland-Japan economic conference to start on October 23 in Tokyo.

- Around 13,000 Belarus-made farm tractors were exported through the Polish ports of Gdansk and Gdynia in the last two years. In future Belarus exporters will use the Lithuanian port of Klaipeda where they have been offered better prices.

- The regulated prices of Polish-made pharmaceuticals have gone up by six percent on average. The rise is below the inflation level and will not hurt patients covered by medication refund scheme, finance ministry officials said.

- Offers to provide credits for small apartments by Polish housing cooperatives, holdings, and developers cannot meet the needs of all people ready to use this year's housing investment tax breaks, Dragowski real estate agency representatives said.
- Almost 62 percent of Poles believe that President Aleksander Kwasniewski serves Poland well, while 25 percent think otherewise, a CBOS polling institute survey showed.

- Pekao SA building society, to start functioning today, will offer housing and apartment modernisation credits. The Food Economy Bank (BGZ), Bank Unii Gospodarczej (BUG), Gospodarczy Bank Poludniowo-Zachodni (GBPZ) and Gospodarczy Bank Wielkopolski (GPW ) plan similar offers soon.
- Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), Poland's telecoms monopolist, will spend an additional 30 million zlotys on wage rises this year, TPSA deputy president Stanislaw Popiolek said.

- The British Know-How Fund will spend 400,000 sterling on modernisation of the Zwoltex blanket and towel maker in Zdunska Wola, central Poland. It will replace the old Italian machines with computer-driven, British-made Longclose equipment.
- Poland's average rye price in the last nine months was 34.88 zlotys, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
